excluded.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > with event observables > should work with an infinite event observable
excluded.reason: fromEventObservable is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the invoked logic is an rxjs interval(10) on a real timer whose values reach the parent as COUNT {value} events, until an eventless transition guarded by count === 5 completes the machine; a host actor settles once and sends its parent nothing else. It would need an event observable logic whose events reach its parent as it produces them

excluded.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > with event observables > should work with a finite event observable
excluded.reason: fromEventObservable is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the invoked logic is an rxjs interval(10).pipe(take(5)) on a real timer that sends its parent COUNT 0 to 4 and then completes, and the invoke's onDone, guarded by count === 4, follows those events; a host actor settles once and sends its parent nothing before its done event. It would need an event observable logic whose events reach its parent and whose completion is its done event

excluded.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > with event observables > should receive an emitted error
excluded.reason: fromEventObservable is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the invoked logic is an rxjs interval(10) on a real timer that sends its parent COUNT 0 to 4 and throws Error('some error') at its sixth value, and the onError guard reads count === 4 and event.error.message; a host actor rejects once and sends its parent nothing before its error event. It would need an event observable logic whose events reach its parent and whose failure is its error event

excluded.test: invoke.test.ts > invoke > with event observables > should work with input
excluded.reason: fromEventObservable is not ported (out of scope for the actor layer): the invoked logic is an rxjs of({type: 'obs.event', value: input}) that sends its parent, when it starts, one event built from its input 42, and a custom action asserts event.value === 42; a host actor only settles, with a done or an error event. It would need an event observable logic that sends its parent an event computed from its input
